To run `ruff` on your project, you would typically execute the command `ruff check .` in the root directory of your project. This will analyze all Python files in the current directory and its subdirectories, checking for syntax errors, style issues, and potential bugs based on the rules defined in `ruff`'s configuration.

The output will list any issues found, including their type (e.g., `E` for error, `F` for fixable, `W` for warning), the line number, and a description of the issue. It may also suggest fixes if applicable. You can review these findings to improve code quality, maintainability, and consistency across your project.
